source.author: stat
source.text: quam ratus, innumeris videt excursare latebris, hos prodire iugis, illos e vallibus imis crescere, nec paucos campo, totumque sub armis collucere iter, ut clausas indagine profert in medium vox prima feras, quae sola medendi turbata ratione via est, petit ardua dirae Sphingos et abscisis infringens cautibus lineas exsuperat iuga dira manus, scopuloque potitus, unde procul tergo metus et via prona nocendi, saxum ingens, quod vix plena cervice gementes vertere humo valeant murisque inferre iuvenci, rupibus evellit; dein toto sanguine nixus sustinet, immanem quaerens librare ruinam, qualis in adversos Lapithas erexit inanem magnanimus cratera Pholus.
source.text_original: quam ratus, innumeris videt excursare latebris, / hos prodire iugis, illos e vallibus imis / crescere, nec paucos campo, totumque sub armis / collucere iter, ut clausas indagine profert / in medium vox prima feras, quae sola medendi / turbata ratione via est, petit ardua dirae / Sphingos et abscisis infringens cautibus lineas / exsuperat iuga dira manus, scopuloque potitus, / unde procul tergo metus et via prona nocendi, / saxum ingens, quod vix plena cervice gementes / vertere humo valeant murisque inferre iuvenci, / rupibus evellit; dein toto sanguine nixus / sustinet, immanem quaerens librare ruinam, / qualis in adversos Lapithas erexit inanem / magnanimus cratera Pholus.
source.text_english: Thinking this is the way, he sees them ranging far and wide from countless hiding places, some emerging from the heights, others rising from the deepest valleys, and not a few across the plain, the whole route glinting under arms; just as the first cry, bringing out the enclosed beasts in a net, is the only way amid a confused hunt to heal the situation. He seeks the steep heights of deadly Sphinx, and, breaking through the cut crags, he climbs beyond the ridges with his ruthless band, and having gained a cliff, where danger lies far behind and the path slopes down to harm, he tears loose a huge boulder, which oxen scarcely groaning with full necks could turn from the ground and carry to the walls; then, leaning on all his strength, he holds it up, seeking to launch a monstrous downfall, like great-souled Pholus raised an empty crater against the hostile Lapiths.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: o si mihi sanguis, quantus erat, cum signiferum cratera minantem non leviore Pholum manus haec compescuit auro, primus in aeratis posuissem puppibus arma concussoque ratem gauderem tollere remo.
reuse.text_original: 'o si mihi sanguis, / quantus erat, cum signiferum cratera minantem / non leviore Pholum manus haec compescuit auro, / primus in aeratis posuissem puppibus arma / concussoque ratem gauderem tollere remo.
reuse.text_english: O if only I had had blood, such as it was when this hand checked Pholus, banner-bearer and threatening with the goblet, not with less gold, I would have been the first to place arms on bronze-clad ships and would have rejoiced to lift the vessel with the shaken oar.
